Specification: This specification models a reconfigurable Paxos-style consensus algorithm with acceptors, ballots, instances, and configurations. It represents acceptor votes in a three-level function `avote` and the set of learned commands in `learned`, including special reconfiguration commands that install new configurations. The file proves safety properties, especially uniqueness of the learned command per instance, by defining a strong inductive invariant, auxiliary configuration-ordering functions, stability lemmas, and a substantial TLAPS proof; there are no liveness or fairness assumptions beyond the standard safety specification `Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<avote, learned>>`.

          /\ \A j\in 0..maxcfg : cfgc[j] = ConfigCmd(cfgC[j])
          /\ learnedRcfg = {cfgl[j] : j \in 0..maxcfg}

ASSUME CONSTANT a \in Acc, 
             CONSTANT c \in Cmd
      PROVE Stable( /\ Voted(a, i, b, C.cnum, c)
                    /\ ConfigOKAt(i, b, C)  )

SUFFICES ASSUME Next, Voted(a, i, b, C.cnum, c), 
                        ConfigOKAt(i, b, C)
                 PROVE  ConfigOKAt(i, b, C)'

SUFFICES ASSUME CONSTANT j \in (ii+1)..(i-1), 
                        CONSTANT c4 \in CCmd,
                        CONSTANT aa \in Acc,
                        ~ Voted(aa, j, b, C.cnum, c4),
                        Voted(aa, j, b, C.cnum, c4)'
                 PROVE  FALSE

ASSUME CONSTANT c1 \in Cmd   \* Bug in parser prevents reuse of symbol c
      PROVE  Stable( /\ ChosenInBal(i, b, C, c1)
                      /\ ConfigOKAt(i, b, C)  )

SUFFICES ASSUME Inv,
                      CONSTANT i \in INum,
                      CONSTANT c1 \in Cmd,
                      CONSTANT c2 \in Cmd,
                      <<i, c1>> \in learned /\ <<i, c2>> \in learned
               PROVE  c1 = c2

SUFFICES ASSUME k < maxcfg
                     PROVE  FALSE

ASSUME ChoosableAt(i, b, C, c),
                 C # cfgC[ Max({j \in 0..maxcfg : cfgi[j] < i}) ]
          PROVE  FALSE
